question:
Which of the following two rivers make 'estuaries'?

a) Narmada

b) Krishna

c) Cauvery

d) Tapi
solution:
The correct answer is __**d-a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada River**:

 
 
• The Narmada River flows westwards and creates an estuary as it meets the Arabian Sea near Bharuch in Gujarat.
 
• It is one of the major rivers in central India, flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
 
• Estuaries are formed where the river meets the sea, mixing fresh and saltwater.
 
 
 
• **Tapi River**:
 
 
• The Tapi River also flows westwards and forms an estuary as it meets the Arabian Sea near Surat in Gujarat.
 
• It is another significant river in central India, flowing through Maharashtra and Gujarat.
 
• Like the Narmada, it mixes fresh and saltwater at its estuary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Estuary**:

 
 
• An estuary is a coastal area where freshwater from rivers and streams meets and mixes with saltwater from the ocean.
 
• Estuaries are highly productive ecosystems, providing habitat for a wide variety of marine life.
 
• They often act as nurseries for many marine species, including fish and shellfish.
 
 
 
• **Westward-flowing Rivers in India**:
 
 
• Besides Narmada and Tapi, other westward-flowing rivers include Sabarmati and Mahi.
 
• These rivers generally flow towards the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **River Mouth**:
 
 
• The mouth of a river is the part where it flows into another water body, such as an ocean, sea, or lake.
 
• River mouths can form various structures, including estuaries, deltas, and rias.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Estuary and Delta**:
 
 
• An estuary is formed by the mixing of river and sea water, while a delta is formed by sediment deposition at the river mouth.
 
• Deltas often have fertile land and support agriculture, whereas estuaries are more saline and support different types of ecosystems.
